The following workaround has been proposed for this problem:

/world is writable persistent storage. Python 3 and /bin/sh are supplied by a read-only runtime. Host research files and the network are unavailable.

Writing in a reply has no automatic filesystem effect. A column-zero line exactly "http://example.org" opens an executable cell. Each reply waits for each physical tick to end.

Initial context contains FRR, these mechanics, the condition law and the initial observation. Every actual reply/feedback pair is retained without pruning until complete input would exceed 7936 tokens. Each reply has up to 256 generated tokens within 8192 total positions. Observation packets have an 8192-byte serialized bound; overflow pauses after known effects are retained. Full raw records remain external; only explicit file operations store writing in /world.

Changing physical law: group field.bin bytes into adjacent pairs (a_i,b_i), with periodic neighbors. Each tick simultaneously sets a_i'=b_i and b_i'=a_i XOR b_(i-1) XOR b_(i+1). XOR is bitwise exclusive
